## Aerial Mysteries Over Tehran
The most compelling visual narrative this week centers on Iran, where OSINT enthusiasts are tracking unusual activity over Tehran. Reports from the OSINTdefender account highlight unidentified objects filmed hovering in the sky, creating an atmosphere of intrigue among observers. This aerial ambiguity is juxtaposed with ground-level evidence: smoke rising from a specific area in western Tehran, suggesting a recent incident or event occurred below.

While videos circulating online do not immediately reveal the nature of the aerial object, the visible smoke adds a layer of urgency. The core of the discussion lies in the potential correlation between these two phenomena. Observers are currently debating whether the mysterious objects are related to the ground disturbance, noting that a clear identification of the object has yet to be confirmed. Until then, the topic remains defined by this stark contrast between ambiguous sky watchers and tangible ground changes.

## Austin’s ICE Street Vigil
In Austin, a dedicated crowd of 300 to 500 protesters occupied the intersection of Research Blvd and Anderson Lane, holding a street vigil to ensure ICE officer Garces Perez remained at the hospital for medical observation. The officer, 28, had shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez while he was making a DoorDash delivery earlier that day. Tensions were already high, as the victim’s family was reportedly initially denied hospital access.

Protesters took matters into their own hands, moving street signs and setting up infrastructure to maintain the vigil, complete with fireworks displays to create a festive yet protective perimeter. Despite their efforts to keep Garces Perez under hospital care for further observation, news outlets confirmed he was released from the hospital into ICE custody. This outcome fulfilled the scenario the community had feared, marking the end of the immediate street blockade but leaving the broader conversation about police accountability and community policing alive.

## Tech Talk: Firefox Boycotts and Claude Code Frustrations
Tech communities are buzzing with both consumer activism and developer criticism. In the /r/firefox subreddit, users are refining strategies to minimize retailer profits. One user, running Firefox 156.0 on Linux Mint, declared Walmart "off-limits" and is seeking technical configurations to block all Walmart cookies entirely, aiming to reduce the retailer's profit from their browsing activity to zero.

Meanwhile, on Bluesky, developers are criticizing Anthropic’s "dogfooding" practices for its Claude Code product. The main complaint targets a new bug-reporting feature that automatically drafts and sends test results to Anthropic at the user's expense. Frustration mounted when the feature failed to send reports twice in one evening, leading to claims that Anthropic "doesn't test their shit, ever." Users contrast this intrusive, self-activating pop-up with competitors like Post Malone’s terminal tool, arguing that Anthropic should let external users consume the tool rather than pretending they are the only ones using it.

## Gaming, Gear, and Nostalgia
Retro gaming enthusiasts are highlighting a rare Game Gear cartridge, *Sonic Drift 2*, specifically noting the track 'Tunnel Tracking Desert Road 2.' Documentation of this handheld title is gaining traction across Bluesky and Tumblr, with @sonichedgeblog leading the charge in showcasing this specific variation.

In photography circles, the motto "gear only matters if your photo doesn't suck" is being debated. Users are revisiting analog history, citing the Minox subminiature spy camera as proof that small form factors and microfilm can yield superior resolution and fine grain compared to modern digital sensors. Finally, nostalgia is alive for Oolong, the Dutch internet artist, with users praising Eric Kessels’ book *In Almost Every Picture* for its whimsical capture of mundane subjects, particularly the beloved "bunny with things on head" motif.

## Quick Hits

*   **Adult Video:** @JAV Titles promoted "Super Cute Beer Vendor Yuki Shiroi Just The Good Bits," a five-hour video highlighting the actress’s aesthetic in a vendor role.
*   **4chan Philosophy:** A /gear/ thread reinforced that technical specs matter most when the composition fails, citing spy cameras as examples of technology packing significant data into small negatives.
*   **Tehran Update:** The debate continues on whether the smoke in western Tehran is linked to the unidentified aerial objects, with no final confirmation yet.
*   **Sonic Fans:** The consensus on the *Sonic Drift 2* Game Gear cartridge is one of pure documentation and appreciation for the specific track listing.

Full frame isn't always better, and in fact for long distance stuff it's usually worse unless you compare a super dense FF sensor to a super sparse APS-C one.

@cANON - /p/ — /gear/ general — >>4529343 It's the same glass, that's the entire point. That a crop camera extends your reach. Same FOV is for equivalence, this was about breaking equivalence. Same FOV with FF means getting a 1280mm setup.

@4529343 - /p/ — /gear/ general — >>4529339 It's disingenuous because it's not apples to apples. If you used a Barlow to bring the FF sensor up to the same FOV as the smaller sensor it would be a fair comparison, but you didn't. What you observed could be attributed to a difference in image scale just as easily, which is dependent on the glass as much as the sensor.

@cANON - /p/ — /gear/ general — >>4529338 It's not disingenous, the point of the debate was that you could get more detail with the same lens by using a denser sensor. Everyone denied it, I proved them wrong. Sensor reach is a thing and more pixels on the target gets you more detail, it should be obvious to anyone who isn't a full frame fanatic.

@Ed (ed3d.net) — sure, but m43 lenses are not THAT much smaller, for sensors that are generally more temperamental: worse light, but also worse denoising at high ISO, etc.  if you were going to maybe go from APS-C standard to M43 stacked, like an OM-3, I could see it, but otherwise I'm not sure it makes sense
